sources.title: Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?

hazards.name: Altered Gravity
hazards.description: Changes in gravity affect the cardiovascular system, muscles, bones, balance, and other body functions.
monitoring_context: Review cardiovascular measurements alongside recent activity.
Use dedicated assessments for muscle and bone health.

hazards.name: Isolation and Confinement
hazards.description: Long-duration isolation, sleep disruption, circadian changes, and workload can affect behavioral health and performance.
monitoring_context: Ask about sleep quality and fatigue.
Use self-reported information alongside cognitive assessments.

hazards.name: Distance from Earth
hazards.description: Long distances and communication delays increase the importance of onboard decision support and crew self-sufficiency.
monitoring_context: Preserve measurements for later medical review.

hazards.name: Hostile or Closed Environments
hazards.description: Spacecraft environmental factors such as atmosphere, pressure, temperature, noise, and microbial conditions can affect crew health.
monitoring_context: Review respiratory indicators in environmental context.
Consider spacecraft air-quality and pressure measurements when available.
Do not infer cabin air quality from physiological telemetry alone.

hazards.name: Space Radiation
hazards.description: Space radiation is an important health hazard requiring dedicated exposure monitoring and protective measures.
monitoring_context: Explain the importance of radiation monitoring.
Use dedicated radiation instruments for exposure measurements.
Do not estimate radiation dose from heart rate or cognitive predictions.

heart.title: Cardiovascular Health
heart.description: Spaceflight-related gravity changes can affect cardiovascular conditioning.
assessment_questions: Were you exercising before this measurement?
Are you experiencing dizziness or unusual fatigue?

lungs.title: Respiratory Health
lungs.description: Respiratory indicators should be interpreted alongside activity and spacecraft environmental conditions.
assessment_questions: Were you physically active before this reading?

brain.title: Cognitive and Behavioral Health
brain.description: Sleep, workload, isolation, and other mission factors can influence crew performance.

bones.title: Musculoskeletal Health
bones.description: Altered gravity can contribute to muscle and bone changes over long missions.
assessment_questions: Have you completed your planned exercise?
Are you experiencing muscle weakness or discomfort?
